request.description:
CASH SALE — Record a sale paid immediately

Records a sale paid by cash, mobile money, or bank. Posts the  
journal entry (4 lines: money in, sales revenue, COGS, stock  
out), creates sale items, and reduces stock. No customer info  
needed — the buyer is anonymous.

Use the same request for cash, MoMo, and bank payments —  
just change paymentMethod.

METHOD: POST  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/sales  
AUTH: Bearer access token (any role — cashiers sell)  
REQUIRES: onboarding completed

BODY:  
{  
"paymentMethod": "cash | mtn_momo | telecel | airtel | bank",  
"items": \[  
{ "productId": "uuid", "quantity": number > 0 }  
\],  
"receiptPrinted": boolean (optional),  
"receiptSentTo": "string (optional, e.g. phone for digital receipt)"  
}

The cashier sends only productId and quantity per item.  
The system looks up prices from the catalogue and computes  
revenue, cost, and profit automatically.

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber, totalRevenue, totalCogs,  
grossProfit, itemCount, isCredit: false, debtorId: null }  
400 → not enough stock for a product  
404 → one or more products not found / inactive  
403 → onboarding not completed  
401 → no/invalid access token

CREDIT SALE — Sell on credit to a NEW customer

Records a sale where the customer pays later. Creates a new  
debtor (the person), posts the journal entry (money goes to  
Debtors, not cash), and creates a debt under that debtor.

Use this when the customer is NEW (not already in the system).  
For a returning customer, use "Old Debtor Credit Sale" instead.

METHOD: POST  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/sales  
AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)  
REQUIRES: onboarding completed

BODY:  
{  
"paymentMethod": "credit",  
"items": \[  
{ "productId": "uuid", "quantity": number > 0 }  
\],  
"customerName": "string (REQUIRED for new credit customer)",  
"customerPhone": "string (optional but encouraged)",  
"dueDate": "string (optional, e.g. 2026-07-01)"  
}

The system creates a debtor record for this customer and a  
debt for the amount owed. The returned debtorId identifies  
this customer — save it to link future credit sales to the  
same person (see Old Debtor Credit Sale).

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber, totalRevenue, totalCogs,  
grossProfit, itemCount, isCredit: true, debtorId }  
400 → credit sale requires a customer name (if none given)  
400 → not enough stock for a product  
404 → one or more products not found / inactive  
403 → onboarding not completed  
401 → no/invalid access token

OLD DEBTOR CREDIT SALE — Sell on credit to an EXISTING customer

Records a credit sale for a customer who is ALREADY in the  
system (a returning credit customer). Instead of creating a  
new debtor, this links the new debt to the existing one — so  
the customer's debts accumulate under a single identity.

Use this when the frontend customer-picker selects an existing  
debtor. Send their debtorId instead of name/phone.

METHOD: POST  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/sales  
AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)  
REQUIRES: onboarding completed

BODY:  
{  
"paymentMethod": "credit",  
"items": \[  
{ "productId": "uuid", "quantity": number > 0 }  
\],  
"debtorId": "uuid (REQUIRED — the existing debtor's ID)",  
"dueDate": "string (optional, e.g. 2026-07-01)"  
}

No customerName needed — debtorId identifies the existing  
customer. The system verifies the debtor belongs to this  
business, then creates a NEW debt under them. The customer  
remains ONE record; their total owed is the sum of all their  
open debts.

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber, totalRevenue, totalCogs,  
grossProfit, itemCount, isCredit: true, debtorId }  
404 → selected customer (debtorId) not found  
400 → not enough stock for a product  
403 → onboarding not completed  
401 → no/invalid access token

PROFIT & LOSS REPORT — Net profit for a period

Returns revenue, COGS, gross profit, expenses (with a per-category  
breakdown), and net profit, computed from the journal for a date  
range. Reads the accounting source of truth, so it always matches  
the books.

METHOD: GET  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/reports/profit-loss  
AUTH: Bearer access token

QUERY PARAMS (all optional):  
from start date, YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-06-01)  
to end date, YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-06-19)

If omitted → defaults to THIS MONTH (1st of current month → today).  
If provided → from must be <= to (else 400).

RESPONSE 200:  
{  
"data": {  
"period": { "from": "2026-06-01", "to": "2026-06-19" },  
"revenue": 8000,  
"cogs": 5000,  
"grossProfit": 3000,  
"expenses": 2500,  
"netProfit": 500,  
"expenseBreakdown": \[  
{ "category": "wages", "name": "Staff wages", "amount": 1200 },  
{ "category": "rent", "name": "Rent", "amount": 500 }  
\]  
}  
}

NOTES:

- Only revenue/COGS/expense accounts affect the P&L. Owner deposits/  
    withdrawals (equity) and opening balance do NOT appear here.
    
- expenseBreakdown is sorted largest-first; categories with 0 are omitted.
    

RESPONSES:  
200 → the report  
400 → invalid range (from after to)  
401 → no/invalid access token  
403 → onboarding not complete

CASH POSITION — Current money on hand

Returns the current balance of every money account (cash, mobile  
money, bank) plus a grand total. A snapshot of "how much money do I  
have right now" — computed from all transactions since the opening  
balance.

METHOD: GET  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/reports/cash-position  
AUTH: Bearer access token

PARAMS: none (it's a current snapshot, not a date range)

RESPONSE 200:  
{  
"data": {  
"asOf": "2026-06-19T...",  
"total": 4700,  
"accounts": \[  
{ "subtype": "cash_hand", "name": "Cash in hand", "balance": 500 },  
{ "subtype": "cash_momo_mtn", "name": "MTN MoMo", "balance": 1200 },  
{ "subtype": "cash_momo_telecel", "name": "Telecel Cash", "balance": 0 },  
{ "subtype": "cash_momo_airtel", "name": "AirtelTigo Money", "balance": 0 },  
{ "subtype": "cash_bank", "name": "Bank account", "balance": 3000 }  
\]  
}  
}

NOTES:

- All 5 money accounts always appear (even at 0), in a fixed order.
    
- Balance = money in (debits) − money out (credits), all time.
    
- This is CASH (money on hand), not profit. Different from the P&L.
    

RESPONSES:  
200 → the cash position  
401 → no/invalid access token  
403 → onboarding not complete

DEBTORS SUMMARY — Who owes you money

Returns customers with outstanding debts, grouped per person, with  
a total. Overdue ones are sorted first. Reads the debts table  
(unpaid only). Answers "who owes me?"

METHOD: GET  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/reports/debtors-summary  
AUTH: Bearer access token

PARAMS: none (current outstanding snapshot)

RESPONSE 200:  
{  
"data": {  
"totalOwed": 1450,  
"count": 3,  
"overdueCount": 1,  
"debtors": \[  
{  
"debtorId": "...",  
"name": "Ama Owusu",  
"phone": "0244...",  
"amountOutstanding": 450,  
"dueDate": "2026-06-10",  
"debtCount": 1,  
"isOverdue": true,  
"isDueSoon": false  
}  
\]  
}  
}

NOTES:

- One row per debtor (their TOTAL across all unpaid debts).
    
- amountOutstanding = sum of that person's unpaid debts.
    
- dueDate = their earliest (most urgent) due date.
    
- Fully-paid debts are excluded.
    
- Sorted: overdue first, then soonest due, then no due date.

CREDITORS SUMMARY — Who you owe

Returns suppliers you owe, grouped per supplier, with a total.  
Reads the payables table (unpaid only). Answers "who do I owe?"

METHOD: GET  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/reports/creditors-summary  
AUTH: Bearer access token

RESPONSE 200:  
{  
"data": {  
"totalOwed": 600,  
"count": 1,  
"overdueCount": 0,  
"creditors": \[  
{  
"creditorId": "...",  
"name": "Tema Wholesale",  
"phone": "...",  
"amountOutstanding": 600,  
"dueDate": "2026-06-30",  
"payableCount": 1,  
"isOverdue": false,  
"isDueSoon": true  
}  
\]  
}  
}

CASH PURCHASE — Buy stock, pay immediately

Records buying inventory paid by cash, mobile money, or bank.  
Stock increases, money goes out. Recomputes each product's  
weighted-average cost and records the latest purchase cost.  
No COGS or profit — that happens later when the stock is sold.

Use the same request for cash, MoMo, and bank — change paymentMethod.

METHOD: POST  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/purchases  
AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)  
REQUIRES: onboarding completed

BODY:  
{  
"paymentMethod": "cash | mtn_momo | telecel | airtel | bank",  
"items": \[  
{ "productId": "uuid", "quantity": number > 0,  
"unitCost": number >= 0 }  
\],  
"notes": "string (optional)"  
}

unitCost is what you paid PER UNIT this time. It updates the  
product's weighted-average cost (used for profit) and is stored  
as the latest purchase cost (shown to help set selling prices).

EFFECT:  
→ product stock INCREASED by quantity  
→ product costPrice = new weighted average  
→ product lastPurchaseCost = this unitCost  
→ journal: DEBIT Stock, CREDIT Cash/MoMo/Bank

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber, totalPurchaseValue, itemCount,  
isCredit: false, creditorId: null }  
404 → one or more products not found / inactive  
403 → onboarding not completed  
401 → no/invalid access token

CREDIT PURCHASE — Buy stock from a NEW supplier on credit

Records buying inventory where you pay the supplier later.  
Stock increases, you now owe the supplier. Creates a new  
creditor (the supplier) and a payable (the amount owed).

Use when the supplier is NEW. For a returning supplier, use  
"Old Creditor Purchase" instead.

METHOD: POST  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/purchases  
AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)  
REQUIRES: onboarding completed

BODY:  
{  
"paymentMethod": "credit",  
"items": \[  
{ "productId": "uuid", "quantity": number > 0,  
"unitCost": number >= 0 }  
\],  
"supplierName": "string (REQUIRED for a new supplier)",  
"supplierPhone": "string (optional)",  
"dueDate": "string (optional, e.g. 2026-07-15)",  
"notes": "string (optional)"  
}

EFFECT:  
→ product stock increased, weighted-avg cost + last cost updated  
→ journal: DEBIT Stock, CREDIT Creditors  
→ creates a creditor (supplier) + a payable (amount owed)

The returned creditorId identifies this supplier — save it to  
link future credit purchases to the same supplier.

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber, totalPurchaseValue, itemCount,  
isCredit: true, creditorId }  
400 → credit purchase requires a supplier name (if none given)  
404 → one or more products not found / inactive  
403 → onboarding not completed

OLD CREDITOR PURCHASE — Buy on credit from an EXISTING supplier

Records a credit purchase from a supplier ALREADY in the system.  
Instead of creating a new creditor, links the new payable to the  
existing one — so the supplier's payables accumulate under a  
single identity (mirrors how repeat credit customers work).

Use when the frontend supplier-picker selects an existing  
creditor. Send creditorId instead of supplierName.

METHOD: POST  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/purchases  
AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)  
REQUIRES: onboarding completed

BODY:  
{  
"paymentMethod": "credit",  
"items": \[  
{ "productId": "uuid", "quantity": number > 0,  
"unitCost": number >= 0 }  
\],  
"creditorId": "uuid (REQUIRED — the existing supplier's ID)",  
"dueDate": "string (optional)",  
"notes": "string (optional)"  
}

No supplierName needed — creditorId identifies the existing  
supplier. The system verifies the creditor belongs to this  
business, then creates a NEW payable under them. The supplier  
remains ONE record; total owed is the sum of their open payables.

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber, totalPurchaseValue, itemCount,  
isCredit: true, creditorId }  
404 → selected supplier (creditorId) not found  
403 → onboarding not completed

LIST PRODUCTS — Get the product catalogue

Returns the business's products. Any authenticated user  
(cashiers need to see products to sell). Defaults to active  
products only.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)

QUERY PARAMS (all optional):  
search → filter by name (e.g. ?search=cowbell)  
categoryId → filter by category  
isActive → 'false' to see deactivated products  
(default shows active only)

RESPONSES:  
200 → array of products (sorted by name)

GET PRODUCT — Get one product by ID

Returns a single product. Any authenticated user.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)

PATH PARAM:  
id → the product's UUID

RESPONSES:  
200 → the product  
404 → product not found (or not in your business)

UPDATE PRODUCT — Edit a product

Updates a product. Owner/manager only. Send only the fields  
you want to change. You cannot change opening quantity here —  
stock changes happen through sales and purchases.

AUTH: Bearer access token (owner or manager)

PATH PARAM:  
id → the product's UUID

BODY (all optional — send only what changes):  
{  
"name": "string",  
"sellingPrice": number,  
"costPrice": number,  
"minimumStockQty": number,  
"unitOfMeasure": "string",  
"sku": "string",  
"categoryId": "uuid or null (null removes the category)"  
}

RESPONSES:  
200 → the updated product  
404 → product or category not found  
400 → validation error  
401/403 → not authenticated / not owner-manager

DEACTIVATE PRODUCT — Soft-delete a product

Sets the product to inactive (isActive = false). This is a  
SOFT delete — the product is hidden from the catalogue but not  
removed, because past sales reference it. Owner/manager only.

AUTH: Bearer access token (owner or manager)

PATH PARAM:  
id → the product's UUID

RESPONSES:  
200 → the deactivated product  
404 → product not found  
401/403 → not authenticated / not owner-manager

OWNER DEPOSIT — Owner puts personal money into the business

Records the owner adding their own money to the business. This  
is NOT income — it increases the owner's capital (equity), not  
profit. Affects cash, not the P&L.

METHOD: POST  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/owner/deposit  
AUTH: Bearer access token

BODY:  
amount number required, > 0  
paymentMethod string required: cash | mtn_momo | telecel | airtel | bank  
notes string optional

JOURNAL EFFECT:  
DEBIT (cash goes up)  
CREDIT Owner capital (owner's stake goes up)

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber (DEP-...), type, amount, paymentMethod }  
400 → amount <= 0, credit not allowed, or stray field  
401 → no/invalid token  
403 → onboarding not complete

OWNER WITHDRAWAL — Owner takes money out for personal use

Records the owner taking money from the business for themselves  
(drawings). This is NOT an expense — it reduces the owner's  
equity, not profit. Affects cash, not the P&L.

METHOD: POST  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/owner/withdrawal  
AUTH: Bearer access token

BODY:  
amount number required, > 0  
paymentMethod string required: cash | mtn_momo | telecel | airtel | bank  
notes string optional

JOURNAL EFFECT:  
DEBIT Owner drawings (drawings up, reduces equity)  
CREDIT (cash goes down)

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber (WDR-...), type, amount, paymentMethod }  
400 → amount <= 0, credit not allowed, or stray field  
401 → no/invalid token  
403 → onboarding not complete

LIST OWNER DEPOSITS — History of money the owner put in

Returns all owner deposits with a running total. Reads from the  
journal. These are equity contributions (not income).

METHOD: GET  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/owner/deposits  
AUTH: Bearer access token

QUERY PARAMS (optional):  
from start date YYYY-MM-DD  
to end date YYYY-MM-DD  
If omitted → returns ALL deposits (all time).

RESPONSE 200:  
{  
"data": {  
"deposits": \[  
{  
"id": "...",  
"referenceNumber": "DEP-2026-00001",  
"date": "2026-06-19",  
"amount": 1000,  
"paymentMethod": "cash",  
"moneyAccount": "Cash in hand",  
"notes": "Added personal funds"  
}  
\],  
"totalDeposited": 1000,  
"count": 1  
}  
}

LIST OWNER WITHDRAWALS — History of money the owner took out

Returns all owner withdrawals (drawings) with a running total.  
Reads from the journal. These reduce equity (not expenses).

METHOD: GET  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/owner/withdrawals  
AUTH: Bearer access token

QUERY PARAMS (optional): from, to (YYYY-MM-DD). Omitted → all time.

RESPONSE 200:  
{  
"data": {  
"withdrawals": \[  
{  
"id": "...",  
"referenceNumber": "WDR-2026-00001",  
"date": "2026-06-19",  
"amount": 500,  
"paymentMethod": "cash",  
"moneyAccount": "Cash in hand",  
"notes": "Personal use"  
}  
\],  
"totalWithdrawn": 500,  
"count": 1  
}  
}

exec: // Sanity check — owner capital should equal assets minus liabilities

request.description:
COMPLETE ONBOARDING — Set opening balances

Posts the business's opening balance as the first journal  
entry and marks onboarding complete. Owner-only, requires  
a valid access token.

METHOD: POST  
AUTH: Bearer access token (required, owner role)

BODY (all fields optional, but TOTAL ASSETS must be > 0):  
{  
"cashInHand": number, // physical cash  
"mtnMomo": number, // MTN mobile money  
"telecel": number, // Telecel cash  
"airtel": number, // AirtelTigo money  
"bankBalance": number, // bank account  
"stockValue": number, // inventory value  
"debtorsTotal": number, // money owed TO the business  
"creditorsTotal": number // money the business OWES  
}

Owner capital is calculated automatically (Assets − Liabilities).

RESPONSES:  
200 → { referenceNumber, ownerCapital, linesPosted, onboardingComplete }  
400 → total assets must be > 0 (can't open with only debts)  
403 → not the owner / no permission  
409 → onboarding already completed  
401 → no/invalid access token

CREATE EXPENSE — Record a business expense

Records money spent on a running cost (rent, wages, transport, etc.).  
Posts a balanced journal entry behind the scenes and stores the  
expense with its details. Paid immediately — no credit.

METHOD: POST  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/expenses  
AUTH: Bearer access token (owner/manager)

BODY FIELDS:

REQUIRED:  
category string the kind of expense (see allowed values)  
amount number amount spent (> 0)  
paymentMethod string how it was paid (see allowed values)

OPTIONAL:  
paidTo string who it was paid to (e.g. "Landlord", "ECG")  
notes string the owner's own note (e.g. "December rent")

ALLOWED VALUES:

category: rent | wages | utilities | transport |  
momo_charges | bank_charges | packaging | other

paymentMethod: cash | mtn_momo | telecel | airtel | bank  
(NO credit — expenses are paid immediately)

EXAMPLE:  
{  
"category": "rent",  
"amount": 500,  
"paymentMethod": "cash",  
"paidTo": "Landlord",  
"notes": "December rent"  
}

MINIMAL (only required):  
{  
"category": "transport",  
"amount": 50,  
"paymentMethod": "cash"  
}

RESPONSES:  
201 → the created expense (id, reference, category, amount, ...)  
400 → validation error (bad/missing field, amount <= 0, or  
paymentMethod "credit" which isn't allowed)  
401 → no/invalid access token  
403 → onboarding not complete

NOTE: "category" maps to an expense account. The category breakdown  
and totals come from these accounts, so net profit = revenue − COGS  
− all expenses is computed from them.

LIST EXPENSES — Get recorded expenses

Returns expenses with totals. Category is derived from each  
expense's account.

METHOD: GET  
URL: {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/expenses  
AUTH: Bearer access token

QUERY PARAMS (all optional):  
category filter to one category (rent, wages, ...)  
from start date (YYYY-MM-DD)  
to end date (YYYY-MM-DD)

RESPONSE 200:  
{  
"data": {  
"expenses": \[  
{  
"id": "...",  
"referenceNumber": "...",  
"date": "...",  
"category": "rent",  
"categoryName": "Rent",  
"amount": 500,  
"paymentMethod": "cash",  
"paidTo": "Landlord",  
"notes": "December rent"  
}  
\],  
"totalSpent": 500,  
"count": 1  
}  
}

LIST DEBTORS — Flexible query for the customer/debt views

Returns the business's debtors, each with their computed total  
owed and open debt count. ONE endpoint that powers several  
different screens via filters. Any authenticated user.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)

QUERY PARAMS (all optional, combine as needed):  
search → filter by name (case-insensitive contains)  
hasDebt → 'true' = only debtors who currently owe  
'false' = only debtors who are fully settled  
isActive → 'false' = deactivated/archived debtors  
(defaults to active debtors when omitted)

USE CASES — how the frontend uses this endpoint:

Customer picker (credit sale):  
GET /debtors?search=kofi  
→ find a specific customer to link a credit sale to

"Who owes me" screen:  
GET /debtors?hasDebt=true  
→ everyone with an outstanding balance, sorted by name

Full customer list:  
GET /debtors  
→ all active credit customers

Settled customers:  
GET /debtors?hasDebt=false  
→ customers who have paid everything off

Archived customers:  
GET /debtors?isActive=false  
→ customers that have been deactivated/hidden

NOTE: isActive (the record's status) and hasDebt (whether they  
owe) are INDEPENDENT. A customer can be active+owing,  
active+settled, or inactive+settled.

RESPONSES:  
200 → array of debtors, each:  
{ id, name, phone, notes, isActive, totalOwed, openDebtCount }

GET DEBTOR — One customer's full debt picture

Returns a single debtor with ALL their debts (oldest first) and  
recent payments, plus computed total owed. Powers the debtor  
detail screen shown before recording a payment.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)

PATH PARAM:  
id → the debtor's UUID

RESPONSES:  
200 → { id, name, phone, notes, isActive, totalOwed,  
debts: \[ {id, amountOriginal, amountOutstanding,  
debtDate, dueDate, status} \],  
recentPayments: \[ {id, amountPaid, paymentMethod,  
paymentDate, notes} \] }  
404 → debtor not found

RECORD PAYMENT — Customer pays toward their debt

Records a payment and applies it across the debtor's open debts  
OLDEST-FIRST (FIFO). Posts the journal (money in, Debtors down)  
and updates each affected debt. Cannot exceed total owed.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)  
REQUIRES: onboarding completed

PATH PARAM:  
id → the debtor's UUID

BODY:  
{  
"amount": number > 0,  
"paymentMethod": "cash | mtn_momo | telecel | airtel | bank",  
"notes": "string (optional)"  
}

The payment clears the oldest debt first, rolling any remainder  
to the next. A fully paid debt → 'paid'; partly paid → 'partial'.

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber, amountPaid, debtsAffected,  
debtsClearedCount, remainingOwed }  
400 → payment exceeds total owed, OR no outstanding debts  
404 → debtor not found  
403 → onboarding not completed

UPDATE DEBTOR — Edit a customer's details

Updates name, phone, or notes. Any authenticated user (cashiers  
deal with customers daily). Send only the fields to change.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)

PATH PARAM:  
id → the debtor's UUID

BODY (all optional):  
{ "name": "string", "phone": "string", "notes": "string" }

RESPONSES:  
200 → the updated debtor  
404 → debtor not found

1. DEACTIVATE DEBTOR — Hide a settled customerSoft-deletes a debtor (isActive = false). Any authenticated  
    user. BLOCKED if the debtor still owes — settle their debts  
    first. Used for list hygiene: removing customers who are gone,  
    duplicates, or mistakes.AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)PATH PARAM:  
    id → the debtor's UUIDRESPONSES:  
    200 → the deactivated debtor  
    400 → debtor still has outstanding debts  
    404 → debtor not found

LIST CREDITORS — Suppliers the business owes

Returns the business's creditors (suppliers), each with the  
computed total owed and open payable count. One flexible endpoint  
serving several screens. Any authenticated user. Defaults to  
active creditors.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)

QUERY PARAMS (all optional, combine as needed):  
search → filter by supplier name (case-insensitive)  
hasDebt → 'true' = only suppliers you currently owe  
'false' = only fully-settled suppliers  
isActive → 'false' = deactivated/archived suppliers  
(defaults to active when omitted)

USE CASES:  
Supplier picker (credit purchase):  
GET /creditors?search=tema  
"Who I owe" screen:  
GET /creditors?hasDebt=true  
Full supplier list:  
GET /creditors  
Settled suppliers:  
GET /creditors?hasDebt=false  
Archived suppliers:  
GET /creditors?isActive=false

NOTE: isActive (record status) and hasDebt (whether you owe them)  
are INDEPENDENT.

RESPONSES:  
200 → array of creditors, each:  
{ id, name, phone, notes, isActive, totalOwed, openPayableCount }

GET CREDITOR — One supplier's full picture

Returns a single creditor with ALL their payables (oldest first)  
and recent payments, plus computed total owed. Powers the  
supplier detail screen shown before paying them.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)

PATH PARAM:  
id → the creditor's UUID

RESPONSES:  
200 → { id, name, phone, notes, isActive, totalOwed,  
payables: \[ {id, amountOriginal, amountOutstanding,  
debtDate, dueDate, status} \],  
recentPayments: \[ {id, amountPaid, paymentMethod,  
paymentDate, notes} \] }  
404 → creditor not found

RECORD PAYMENT — Pay a supplier

Records a payment TO a supplier and applies it across their open  
payables OLDEST-FIRST (FIFO). Posts the journal (Creditors down,  
money out) and updates each affected payable. Cannot exceed what  
you owe.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)  
REQUIRES: onboarding completed

PATH PARAM:  
id → the creditor's UUID

BODY:  
{  
"amount": number > 0,  
"paymentMethod": "cash | mtn_momo | telecel | airtel | bank",  
"notes": "string (optional)"  
}

The payment clears the oldest payable first, rolling any remainder  
to the next. A fully paid payable → 'paid'; partly paid → 'partial'.

EFFECT (journal — opposite of a debtor payment):  
DEBIT Creditors (you owe less)  
CREDIT Cash/MoMo/Bank (money leaves)

RESPONSES:  
201 → { referenceNumber, amountPaid, payablesAffected,  
payablesClearedCount, remainingOwed }  
400 → payment exceeds what you owe, OR no outstanding debts  
404 → creditor not found  
403 → onboarding not completed

UPDATE CREDITOR — Edit a supplier's details

Updates name, phone, or notes. Any authenticated user. Send only  
the fields to change.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)

PATH PARAM:  
id → the creditor's UUID

BODY (all optional):  
{ "name": "string", "phone": "string", "notes": "string" }

RESPONSES:  
200 → the updated creditor  
404 → creditor not found

DEACTIVATE CREDITOR — Hide a settled supplier

Soft-deletes a creditor (isActive = false). Any authenticated  
user. BLOCKED if you still owe them — settle what you owe first.  
Used for list hygiene: removing suppliers you no longer use.

AUTH: Bearer access token (any role)

PATH PARAM:  
id → the creditor's UUID

RESPONSES:  
200 → the deactivated creditor  
400 → you still owe this supplier money  
404 → creditor not found

SIGNUP — Create a new business account

Creates a business, its owner user, and the full chart of  
accounts (25 accounts) in one atomic operation. Returns an  
access token and a refresh token (both auto-saved by the  
test script).

After signup, onboardingComplete is false — the user must  
complete onboarding (set opening balances) next.

METHOD: POST  
AUTH: None

BODY (all fields required):  
{  
"businessName": "string",  
"businessType": "see allowed values",  
"ownerName": "string",  
"phoneNumber": "string (min 10 digits)",  
"locationRegion": "string",  
"locationDistrict": "string",  
"tier": "tier1 | tier2",  
"recordingMode": "daily_summary | transaction",  
"email": "valid email",  
"password": "string (min 8 chars)"  
}

businessType allowed values:  
provision_store, supermarket, pharmacy, spare_parts,  
hardware, boutique, wholesale, cosmetics, electronics,  
stationery, phone_accessories, other

RESPONSES:  
201 → { accessToken, refreshToken, business, user }  
409 → email already exists  
400 → validation error (missing/invalid fields)

VERIFY EMAIL

Confirms the 6-digit code sent during signup. On success, marks the  
account verified, seeds the chart of accounts, and issues access +  
refresh tokens (this is where the user is logged in).

METHOD: POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email  
AUTH: none

BODY:  
email string required, the signup email  
code string required, the 6-digit OTP from the email

RESPONSES:  
200 → { accessToken, refreshToken, business, user(emailVerified:true) }  
400 → incorrect code / expired / no active code  
409 → email already verified  
429 → too many failed attempts (request a new code)

RESEND VERIFICATION

Sends a fresh verification code to an unverified account. Returns a  
neutral response regardless of whether the account exists or is already  
verified (prevents account enumeration). Rate-limited.

METHOD: POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification  
AUTH: none

BODY:  
email string required

RESPONSES:  
200 → neutral "If the account exists, a new code has been sent."  
(a new code is emailed only if an UNVERIFIED account exists)  
429 → rate limit exceeded (max requests per window)

NOTE: a new code invalidates any previous code for that account.

FORGOT PASSWORD

Starts the password-reset flow. If a VERIFIED account exists for the  
email, a 6-digit reset code is emailed. Returns a neutral response  
regardless (prevents account enumeration). Rate-limited.

METHOD: POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password  
AUTH: none

BODY:  
email string required

RESPONSES:  
200 → neutral "If the account exists, a reset code has been sent."  
(reset code emailed only if a VERIFIED account exists)  
429 → rate limit exceeded

NOTE: unverified accounts cannot reset (they never finished signup) —  
the response is still neutral, but no email is sent.

RESET PASSWORD

Confirms the reset code and sets a new password. On success, updates the  
password and REVOKES ALL existing sessions (the user must log in again  
everywhere with the new password). Rate-limited.

METHOD: POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password  
AUTH: none

BODY:  
email string required  
code string required, 6-digit reset code from email  
newPassword string required, min 8 characters

RESPONSES:  
200 → "Password reset successfully. Please log in with your new password."  
400 → incorrect code / expired / no active code / weak password  
429 → too many failed attempts

SECURITY: all refresh tokens are revoked on success — every device is  
logged out and must re-authenticate with the new password.

LOGIN — Authenticate and get tokens

Verifies credentials using the chosen strategy and returns  
a fresh access + refresh token pair (auto-saved by the test  
script).

METHOD: POST  
AUTH: None

BODY:  
{  
"strategy": "email_password",  
"email": "valid email",  
"password": "string"  
}

Currently only "email_password" strategy is available.  
google_oauth and phone_otp are planned.

RESPONSES:  
200 → { accessToken, refreshToken, business, user }  
401 → invalid email or password  
403 → account deactivated

REFRESH — Get a new access token

Exchanges a valid refresh token for a NEW access + refresh  
token pair (rotation). The old refresh token is revoked.  
Call this automatically when any request returns 401 due to  
an expired access token.

IMPORTANT: refresh tokens are single-use. Each refresh  
returns a new pair — replace both on the client.

METHOD: POST  
AUTH: None (the refresh token in the body IS the auth)

BODY:  
{  
"refreshToken": "string"  
}

RESPONSES:  
200 → { accessToken, refreshToken, business, user }  
401 → invalid/expired token, OR reuse detected (all the  
user's tokens get revoked — user must log in again)

LOGOUT — End the current session (one device)

Revokes the given refresh token. The access token will still  
work until it expires (max 15 min) but cannot be refreshed.

METHOD: POST  
AUTH: None (refresh token in body)

BODY:  
{  
"refreshToken": "string"  
}

RESPONSES:  
200 → logged out

LOGOUT ALL — End all sessions (every device)

Revokes ALL of the user's refresh tokens across every device.  
Use for "sign out everywhere", stolen device, or after a  
password change. Requires a valid access token.

METHOD: POST  
AUTH: Bearer access token (required)

BODY: none

RESPONSES:  
200 → logged out of all devices  
401 → no/invalid access token
